predecessor.packageDigest264Note: sha256 of verification/expert-hazlenz-264-.../REPORT-264.sha256, recomputed from the file at §265 and matching the value the §265 authorization carried. verification/current/EXPERT-HAZLENZ-STATE.json recorded 0be6f8c33bc494cf0bf50440de4a3a933f3a00843e09183ed674358c596bfdae for §264, which does NOT reproduce; the §264 package itself verifies clean under `shasum -c REPORT-264.sha256` (4/4 OK), so the frozen bytes are intact and only the living index carried a value that cannot be derived from them. Recorded here rather than silently replaced.

newRoute.why: a browser holds nothing after a reload. Without a read the only ways to learn an analysis's state are to re-execute it — two provider legs to answer a question the database already answers — or to keep believing a cached copy. The second is how a settled conclusion gets rendered from stale client state.

responseContractAdditions.confirmationSubjectUnresolvableIsNamedNo: resolvable:false with a refusal code is a different fact from 'there is nothing to confirm', and only one of them means the confirm control must be withdrawn

effectiveDecisionRelocation.why: the first real consumer is InspectionService.finalizeFinding, and ExpertHazLenzProductModule already imports InspectionModule. Leaving the derivation there would have forced the consumer to re-derive authority locally to escape the module cycle — the exact failure deriveEffectiveDecision exists to prevent, arriving through the module graph rather than through carelessness. One implementation remains; it is now reachable from both sides.

downstreamConsumer.whySelected: the first point in the existing product flow where an Expert posture stops being analysis and becomes a consequential product fact: finalization writes the finding the report reads and, on the finalized branch, creates a corrective action whose urgency derives from that conclusion. §260 section 11 froze it as BLOCKED pre-confirmation.
downstreamConsumer.refusalSentenceSource: the derivation's own statement, not one composed at the consumer

frontendChanges.relationshipToTheLegacyPath: ADDITIVE. The deterministic analysis is unchanged and still rendered in full beneath the Expert panel. saveAnalysisSnapshot is NOT used for Expert and a source check fails if it ever is — routing a server-authored result through the legacy client-supplied path would hand the client authorship of the thing that makes Expert trustworthy.

clientSideAuthorityLogic.confirmationRequired: read from the response; never assigned in the client
clientSideAuthorityLogic.confirmationSubject: server-derived; the client renders it and never computes it
clientSideAuthorityLogic.answerVocabulary: served in answerOptions. An empty list offers no answers rather than falling back on a hardcoded pair, because a client-held vocabulary that drifts from the server's is a reviewer answering in words the server will reject or misread.
clientSideAuthorityLogic.unrecognisedStateRendersAs: UNRECOGNISED, with no content — never as an available analysis
clientSideAuthorityLogic.guardWasNegativelyTested: mayPresentAsSettled was temporarily replaced with `read.analysisState === "ANALYSIS_CONFIRMED"`; the check failed with 2 errors and exit 1, then passed again once reverted. It is a live guard rather than a decoration.

frontendChanges.loadingBehaviour: the held result is dropped BEFORE the request goes out, so no previous analysis is on screen while a new one is in flight. The running view renders its own message and nothing else — no hazards, no posture, no partial result.
frontendChanges.failedStateReachability: ANALYSIS_FAILED exists only on the execution response, because a provider failure writes no analysis row. The execution response is ADAPTED into the read shape (readFromExecution) and passed through the SAME total state map, rather than through a second presenter that could drift.
internalVocabularySuppressed: the candidate hash as primary UX
frontendChanges.provenanceSurface: a collapsed 'Show analysis record' details panel, never the headline
frontendChanges.idempotency: the key is derived from the observation and the action and is reused on retry, so an accidental double-click or a retried fetch resolves to the execution that already ran. It increments only when the inspector deliberately asks again after a failure.

acceptance.caseKIsFrontendOnly: a browser rendering rule cannot be proven by a server suite. The server suite proves the server said the conclusion is unsettled; case K proves the browser does not turn that into a conclusion anyway.

staleExpectationCorrectedBeforeExecution.wasExpected: ANALYSIS_AVAILABLE or ANALYSIS_AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, per §260's design table
staleExpectationCorrectedBeforeExecution.whyNotADefect: §252 gave PRESERVE_UNRESOLVED precedence deliberately after §260's table was written, so both the contained shape and the whole-output shape surface as ANALYSIS_UNRESOLVED. The current-state document records this as accepted v1.0 limitation 3.
staleExpectationCorrectedBeforeExecution.whatWasDoneInstead: §265 asserts the behaviour the product actually has, and CHECKS the limitation's own claim rather than repeating it: G-5 measures that the two shapes remain distinguishable in the record. They are — F carries postureRefusalCodes [] and G carries ["DECLARATION_NOT_COVERED"], with admission PRESERVE_UNRESOLVED on both.

deliberatelyNotDone.reviewerRevisionOfASettledAnalysis: PRODUCT DECISION DEFERRED. One settlement per analysis in the beta workflow. Not a claim that irreversibility is permanent product policy.
deliberatelyNotDone.remainingDownstreamGuards: five of the six §260 section 11 consumers are contained by the finalization gate rather than guarded in their own right
deliberatelyNotDone.findingReconciliationFromAnExpertAnalysi: still zero; §265 added a refusal, not a creation
deliberatelyNotDone.governedEvidenceLoader: unchanged; Expert still transmits zero governed records and may cite nothing
deliberatelyNotDone.hostedProviderCall: zero; every leg was answered by the substituted deterministic transport
